title: Scáth, the Wandering City
summary: A hidden city that moves and vanishes, sought by Cainite coteries.

claims.text: Scáth is said to shift its position and drop from sight at times, so no map can find it; seekers expect ancient mystic treasures there and a secret about the Blood itself.
A diary of 1242 tells of a coterie sent by an unnamed powerful patron, chasing clues through Dublin, Edinburgh and Norwich toward London.

title: The Road-Hunger of the Seekers
summary: How the patron's gift changed the seekers' thirst.

claims.text: On the hunt for Scáth the travellers stopped needing blood: those who kept to the path felt fed, while those who strayed starved as if a week without a vessel.
Childer Embraced on the road shared the gift, did not hunger and did not turn on their sires when they rose.
In Edinburgh a woman gave the coterie an ancient clawed fingerbone that killed plants within a foot and had already killed three horses that carried it.

title: Abyss Mystics
summary: Lasombra who study the darkness as a path of worship and power.

claims.text: A small number of Lasombra scholars gaze into darkness to find secrets, servants and gods; they offer to entropy and gain powers to confuse, terrify and destroy.
The rest of the clan treats them with both respect and distance, and few Lasombra wish to follow them.
Their underground sanctums are called Oubliettes; Boukephos of Clan Lasombra broke with this and raised one on the surface.

title: The Ingurgitant Vortex
summary: An Abyss Mystic's trap painted in blood.

claims.text: The mystic paints a spiral costing two blood points per metre, prays to the Abyss for an hour in sight of it and spends two Willpower, then rolls Manipulation + Occult at difficulty 6; each success keeps the vortex for two turns.
A botch bars the mystic from summoning Abyssal beings for seven nights.
The mystic senses anyone near the sigil and whether mortal or Cainite; one blood point makes the vortex attack and drag victims into the Abyss for nights equal to the mystic's Obtenebration.

title: Assamite Concealment Rite
summary: A blood rite that hides a place from travellers.

claims.text: The sorcerer circles in blood, anoints the head, lies facing the sky, and must reach shelter before sunrise; the rite drains all but one blood point by waking.
For a month, anyone within half a mile goes around the spot or passes it unseeing, and tracks to and from it vanish; done inside Alamut it covers all of Alamut.

title: Koldunism in the Voivodate
summary: The spirit-pact sorcery of the Tzimisce lands.

claims.text: Rivals blame the Tzimisce grip on Hungaria, Poland and Bulgaria on bonds with earth spirits: the Telyavs speak of primordial demons, and the Tremere of Ceoris of wicked ancient spirits.
Koldunism, like Necromancy, claims old pagan roots, so Cainites rate it above Hermetic ritual.

title: Evoke the Storm
summary: A Level Four Transylvanian kraina rite.

claims.text: From a high open place with a clear horizon the koldun can raise gales, lightning and storms anywhere in view, short of a hurricane; player and Storyteller agree the effect.
This lasting rite is lost if the koldun ever stays awake past dawn.

title: The Witches of Echidna
summary: Setite sorcerers who once sold their art across the Mediterranean.

claims.text: Through the Long Night these sorcerers worked for courts from Iberia to Constantinople, and their blood magic, older than the Tremere, won the Serpents sanctuary and places at court.
By the War of Princes Setites are mostly unwelcome, the Witches have faded, and Setite Sorcery is kept from other clans.
Akhu is the Egyptian name for Setite Sorcery; its cults follow many gods but share one aim, to strengthen the clan and find and please its founder.
Mortal scholars place learned high magic of philosophy and mystery cults above the low magic of hearth and countryside, where folk faith and nature worship blend.
The Order of Hermes takes low secrets where it can, and other practitioners are pushed to join as a House or perish.
Cainites invert this: they think better of witchcraft than mortals do and worse of Hermetic ritual, which they tie to the usurping Tremere; nearly everyone hates devil worshippers.

title: Keeping Holdings Across Lifetimes
summary: How the undead keep land in a mortal world.

claims.text: A Cainite may be, or pose as, the rightful lord or vassal of valuable holdings, and must plan for them to stay in hand as mortal faces age.
Staying too long draws the Church's notice to unnatural good health, and failing to pass holdings smoothly to a childe or puppet can lose everything.
Some forge papers and a past and start over in another country, at the cost of fury if found out.

title: Knighthood
summary: The mounted warriors of the age.

claims.text: Most knights are of noble birth with some clerical schooling; they train from youth, and the less able buy out of service through scutage or fall into poverty.
Commoners rarely win knighthood on the field; they serve war by feeding knights.
Landed knights owe about forty days of military service.

Side Slam: from a walk, trot or canter, Dexterity + Ride at difficulty 6 hits up to three adjacent foes from a warhorse, two from a riding horse; it may only be dodged, deals the horse's Strength as bashing, and knocks prone anyone whose Strength the damage beats.
Unhorse: Strength + Brawl or Melee at +2 difficulty from horseback; successes equal to the rider's Strength dismount the target on top of the damage.
Some were knighted before the Embrace; others join a Cainite chivalric order or are dubbed under the shadow feudalism of the Damned.
Cainite knightly orders began as novelties and became traditions, and many have risen and fallen.

title: The Templars
summary: A military order beyond Cainite reach.

claims.text: The order is rich and known for meddling, sides with Saracens when it suits, and lends money in spite of the usury ban.
Its inner circle has always resisted Cainite subversion; meddlers burn, and rumour says supremely faithful warrior priests lead it and list night creatures to be judged on a future day.

title: Eye for the Weakness of Steel
summary: A combination Discipline of Auspex 1, Celerity 1 and Fortitude 1.

claims.text: Toreador and Ventrue of the Fellowship of Our Lady developed it, and it passed to their successors after the Fellowship broke apart in 1218 through infighting.
Each blood point spent lets one blow ignore three soak dice of ordinary armour on one foe; it is reflexive and lasts the scene.

title: The Followers of Nikolas
summary: A cult of faithful Cainites watched by Moncada.

claims.text: The cult outlived Nikolas and never learned who set the inquisitor on it; Moncada knows it survived and tracks it, holding back for now, perhaps aware that striking before turned Nikolas into a martyr.
Blood Apocrypha, Guardian Vigil and Mask of a Thousand Faces are favoured among them, along with combination Disciplines of their own.
Most members are truly devout, though like any faith it draws frauds.

title: The Faithful Damned
summary: Cainites who keep faith despite the curse.

claims.text: Some Cainites hold that they are not souls bound for Hell, and turn toward the light that burns them even with the Beast within.
Demons seldom show as horned devils; they wear the look of a friend, lover or confidant, and the strongest pose as gods.
All are unholy and all want something, and one may keep company with a Cainite for years before naming its price.
